title: Lotus Bridge - Private VPC onramp + split-horizon DNS evaluation
summary: Initial discovery focusing on Lotus Bridge's network constraints for a private deployment of Redwood: strict egress IP whitelisting, split-horizon DNS in a multi-account AWS setup, preference for Private Endpoints but evaluating Transit Gateway peering for cross-region traffic, and SOC2/KMS requirements. AE/SE to provide design doc, security pack, and a bench plan for perf tests in their non-prod region.
action_items: Danilo - draft proposed VPC peering + Private Endpoint topology and upload diagram to shared drive - due 2027-11-10
Priya - share compliance checklist and confirm whether HSM required or cloud KMS acceptable - due 2027-11-09
Alex - provide VPC IDs, CIDR ranges, and account IDs for non-prod and prod - due 2027-11-08
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs (SOC2 cert, pen test summary, KMS integration notes)
Schedule walkthrough of proposed topology with Lotus Bridge network team next Tuesday 11/09
Run a small benchmark using Redwood Hosted in Lotus Bridge non-prod region to validate latency and egress behaviour
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-05T16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Danilo Ruiz (Redwood SE), Tess Howard (Redwood Solutions Eng), Alex Park (Lotus Bridge - Platform), Priya Shah (Lotus Bridge - Security), Raj Menon (Lotus Bridge - Network), Sam (SRE)

[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the account lead, with me is Danilo and Tess from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Alex: Good, yeah thanks. Got a hard stop around 1:05p PST, but should be fine.
[00:00:17] Priya: hey all, Priya here, want to make sure we cover compliance plus the HSM question.
[00:00:22] Danilo: great, high-level plan is to understand your networking posture, region constraints, and security requirements then we can map to Private vs Dedicated flows. we'll also talk split-horizon DNS and egress/IPs.
[00:00:35] Raj: quick context: we've got multi-account AWS. Prod in us-west-2, non-prod in us-west-1. We use AWS Transit Gateway in some accounts, but not everywhere. We run split-horizon DNS for internal redirection, and any external egress must go through our egress appliance and be whitelisted by partners.
[00:00:49] Tess: ok thanks Raj. just to check, when you say egress appliance, is that a fixed NAT IP range or egress through a partner?
[00:00:56] Raj: fixed NAT, we've got a small set of static IPs. partners expect those IPs to be whitelisted.
[00:01:02] Maya: gotcha. that's common. Redwood can provide fixed egress IPs for Dedicated, and for Private deployments you can route through your NAT (we support bringing your own egress).
[00:01:12] Sam: is there a difference in how Private endpoints handle egress vs PrivateLink? we've been leaning to Private Endpoints because of cross-account trust complexity.
[00:01:20] Danilo: good question. quick distinction: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) give you an ENI in your VPC that routes to our service; Private Endpoints (terminology varies) — our private-onprem package creates direct endpoints inside customer's network via private connectivity. For your multi-account setup, PrivateLink is often simpler than cross-account peering or Transit Gateway, but if you need low-latency cross-region, Transit Gateway peering might be better.
[00:01:45] Priya: our concern is also DNS. with split-horizon we need internal names to resolve to internal endpoints, but external names to go to public endpoints for monitoring. How do you handle split-horizon?
[00:01:55] Danilo: we support custom DNS ack — sorry, forwarding. Typical pattern: create private hosted zones in your account, then set up Route53 Resolver inbound endpoints to forward our service domain to your VPC, or conversely forward from your VPC to our resolver. There's a few patterns; we can diagram.
[00:02:09] Raj: do you need outbound access to 3rd party telemetry or anything? we'd prefer all traffic be egressed through our appliance for auditing.
[00:02:15] Maya: we can configure the agents to use your egress; for Hosted API calls Redwood typically originates egress from our infra, but in Private deployment the runtime runs in your VPC so all outbound follows your NAT. For Dedicated there is an option to lock egress and route through customer-provided egress (BYOE).
[00:02:30] [00:02:31] Speaker 6 (maybe mislabelled): mm-hmm
[00:02:35] Alex: on the latency front — we're doing realtime embeddings at ~200ms requirement for some user-facing features. Does Private in our region support that latency?
[00:02:43] Danilo: depends on model size and instance type. For embeddings small models are fine; for larger LLMs latency depends on GPU type and NVLink. For Private, you control instance sizing. For Dedicated we can recommend a profile that meets 200ms for your QPS. We'll add a perf plan.
[00:02:58] Priya: about keys — we store customer data tokenization keys in AWS KMS. Does Redwood integrate with customer KMS or require vault/HSM?
[00:03:06] Tess: Redwood supports cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can integrate with external HSMs. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS and we use customer-managed keys for encrypting at rest. We'll include the KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[00:03:20] Raj: any requirement for private link vs peering for cross-account? our prod account is separate; we don't want to open peering across lots of accounts.
[00:03:28] Danilo: PrivateLink reduces cross-account network surface because it's an endpoint in your account; peering or Transit Gateway requires more routing config. If you already use Transit Gateway across accounts, connecting the Redwood VPC to TGW might be easiest. There's tradeoffs: TGW can carry multiple services and scale but has additional cost and maintenance.
[00:03:47] Alex: vendor partners also demand IP-level allowlists — so if Redwood is calling external services during model scoring (e.g., safety webhooks), we need to know those ranges.
[00:03:56] Maya: we'll provide a list of outbound IP ranges for Hosted and for any Managed Dedicated egress. For Private where you're running the runtime, outbound is your responsibility — we only call third-party webhooks if you configure those integrations. We'll provide a workbook with IPs and webhook behaviors.
[00:04:11] [00:04:12] Alex: cool. can you talk through how upgrades/rollouts work in Private? we need canarying and rollback ability.
[00:04:17] Danilo: yes, our control plane (for Private deployments that opt in) manages versions and can perform canary traffic splits. For fully air-gapped installs, upgrades are manual but we provide a package with checks. For a hybrid Private (control plane in Redwood, runtime in your VPC) you get canaries and A/B rollouts similar to Hosted.
[00:04:34] Priya: audit logs - we need admin actions, token usage, and model change logs forwarded to our central SIEM. Is that available?
[00:04:41] Tess: yes, audit streaming is supported. For Private we can push logs to your S3 or onto an event collector via Kinesis/CloudWatch forwarder. We'll include sample schemas.
[00:04:52] Raj: how do you recommend handling split-horizon for the service FQDN? we currently own internal zone lotus.internal and public lotus.com. Would you require a new zone?
[00:04:59] Danilo: often customers create a private hosted zone like redwood.private.lb-lotus and then use Route53 Resolver rules to forward queries for redwood.example.com to their internal records. Another option is to use conditional forwarders from our resolver to your VPC. We'll lay out both patterns in the diagram.
[00:05:14] Alex: is there a way to do TLS termination inside our VPC so certificates are controlled by us?
[00:05:19] Danilo: yes. For Private we can terminate TLS at customer's edge. For PrivateLink the connection is ENI-based and you still get TLS to the service; mutual TLS can be configured. We support customer-provided certs via ACM or by mounting certs in runtime.
[00:05:33] Priya: any SOC2 artifacts we can get now?
[00:05:36] Maya: yes we'll share SOC2 Type II, pentest summary, and our data processing addendum. Also a KMS/HSM integration note and our RBAC docs.
[00:05:44] Raj: one more network nit: do you support asymmetric routing across TGW? we have some regional appliances that expect return traffic from the same path.
[00:05:52] Danilo: we can recommend path pinning and ensure the runtime source IPs are predictable. In Dedicated we provide egress elasticity but can pin public egress addresses if needed. For Private the source is your NAT so you control it.
[00:06:05] [00:06:06] Speaker 1: okay
[00:06:08] Alex: how intrusive is the Private install — do we need to open any inbound ports to our prod VPC from Redwood?
[00:06:14] Danilo: Private install with the hybrid control plane uses PrivateLink/ENIs so you won't open inbound from Redwood's networks; you'll create ENIs or route to our runtime. For Dedicated there will be a managed VPC but you can peer or use PrivateLink. We'll avoid opening broad inbound access.
[00:06:30] Priya: curious about data residency — we have users in EU and have to keep inference artifacts in-region. Do you support multi-region private deployments?
[00:06:37] Tess: yes, we support multi-region Private deployments. Customers often deploy a regional runtime in each region and the control plane handles routing. For the control plane we can also offer a private control plane in your VPC (on-prem) if you need full isolation.
[00:06:50] Raj: we'd like to see a simple topology for: 1) non-prod in us-west-1 via PrivateLink, 2) prod in us-west-2 via TGW to avoid many link endpoints. Is that doable?
[00:06:59] Danilo: absolutely. We'll sketch a hybrid topology: PrivateLink for isolated non-prod accounts, TGW attachment for prod with expected CIDR and route maps. We'll include NAT/pat ranges and Route53 Resolver config.
[00:07:12] Alex: load testing: can we spin up a trial to validate 200ms embeddings? we can provide sample traffic profile.
[00:07:18] Maya: yes we'll propose a bench: Redwood Hosted in us-west-1 for quick smoke then Dedicated profile or Private runtime in your non-prod account for a controlled run. We'll need sample prompts, QPS targets, and acceptable p99 latency.
[00:07:30] Priya: what about secrets management for model keys and prompts? we want to avoid secrets being logged.
[00:07:36] Tess: we use secret managers and never persist plaintext into logs. For Private you can supply your secret provider. We'll show the log redaction behavior in the security pack.
[00:07:48] [00:07:49] Raj: how about service discovery — will instances register in our existing Consul cluster?
[00:07:54] Danilo: we don't require Consul; but if you want the runtime to register locally we can provide hooks or sidecars to register.
[00:08:02] Alex: timeline constraints: we have a compliance gate mid-December, decision by 12/15, pilot in Jan. Can you support that?
[00:08:09] Maya: yes that timeline is reasonable. we'll aim to deliver docs and bench plan in the next week to keep you on track for the compliance gate.
[00:08:17] Priya: any known gotchas for Route53 Resolver endpoints across accounts? we've had issues with resolver rules not applying for certain VPC attachments.
[00:08:24] Danilo: yes it's a common pain. We'll provide a checklist: ensure correct inbound/outbound resolver endpoints, cross-account IAM permissions for Route53 Resolver rules, and ensure the TGW isn't intercepting DNS.
[00:08:37] Raj: ok, then specific asks from our side: sample topology diagrams, list of IPs for egress (for Hosted/Dedicated), KMS integration guide, and audit log schemas.
[00:08:46] Maya: we'll send those. Danilo, Tess, do you want to add?
[00:08:50] Tess: we'll also include a recommended subnet sizing and ENI limits per AZ and notes on security groups for PrivateLink.
[00:08:58] Danilo: and I'll include a perf checklist and the exact steps for setting up Route53 forwarding plus sample Terraform snippets.
[00:09:07] [00:09:08] Alex: sweet. last quick: what SLA can we expect for Private?
[00:09:12] Maya: for Redwood Private with dedicated support we offer enterprise SLAs on the control plane availability; for runtime (when self-hosted) SLA is based on customer infra, but for Dedicated deployments we have SLA-backed latency and uptime. We'll include the SLA matrix.
[00:09:25] Priya: can you also indicate which logs include model input/outputs? that's a blocker for GDPR/data retention concerns.
[00:09:32] Tess: by default we don't store full model inputs long-term. We'll show retention windows and options to disable input capture. For EU workloads we can set shorter retention or disable capture entirely.
[00:09:45] Maya: ok great — quick recap: Redwood to share security pack (SOC2, pentest, KMS notes), networking diagrams for both PrivateLink and TGW, egress IP lists, perf bench plan. Lotus Bridge to share VPC IDs and CIDRs and confirm HSM requirement. We'll meet next week to walk the topology.
[00:10:05] Alex: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[00:10:09] Priya: thanks.
[00:10:11] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs in the next 48 hours.

[00:10:20] --- auto-generated topics (may be partial): private endpoints, route53, private link, transit gateway, egress ip allowlist, kms

[00:10:30] --- possible action items (auto): send SOC2, send network diagrams, schedule follow-up
